    "evidence": "Root cause / sink: IOUtils.java, method unzip(String,String) \u2014 specifically line 124 `File destFile = new File(newPath, currentEntry);` where `currentEntry = entry.getName()` (line 122) is the untrusted ZipEntry name coming straight from the archive's central directory, and line 126/129 `destFile.getParentFile().mkdirs()` which creates arbitrary parent directories derived from that untrusted path before any write occurs.     "regression_hint": "Invariant: for every ZipEntry processed in IOUtils.unzip(), the resolved destination file path (after resolving `..`, `.`, symlinks, and OS-specific separators) must be a descendant of (or exactly equal to) the canonical extraction root; if it is not, unzip must reject/skip that entry (throw or continue) before performing any filesystem mutation \u2014 neither `destinationParent.mkdirs()` (line 129) nor `new FileOutputStream(destFile)` (line 141) may execute against a path outside the root. A correct fix should validate using canonical paths (e.g., `File.getCanonicalPath()` / `Path.normalize()` plus a `startsWith(root + separator)` check, or `Path.relativize`/`Path.startsWith` on normalized paths) rather than naive string checks, and must apply to both the directory-creation call site and the file-write call site since they share the same tainted `destFile`. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: (a) simple `../` traversal (as used in this PoV) and multi-level `../../../etc/...`; (b) absolute-path entry names (e.g. `/etc/cron.d/evil` or `C:\\\\...` on Windows) that ignore `extractFolder` entirely when passed to `new File(base, absoluteChild)`; (c) mixed/alternate separators (`..\\\\`) on platforms where both separators are honored; (d) traversal hidden inside a directory-entry name (`entry.isDirectory()` true) that still reaches `destinationParent.mkdirs()` before the file-write guard would even run; (e) symlink-based escapes where a legitimately-named entry writes through a pre-existing symlink inside the extraction root that points outside it (canonicalization/realpath check handles this too).
